import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import root, least_squares, fsolve
n=150000; l=n-7
h0=np.log(n)-10
g0=-np.log(n)-10

def props(x):
    q,r=x
    r1=r; rrest=(1-r1)/6
    # high probs q*r_i
    # low b=(1-q)/l
    rs=np.r_[r1, np.full(6,rrest)]
    a=q*rs
    b=(1-q)/l
    H=-q*np.sum(rs*np.log(a)) - (1-q)*np.log(b)  # Wait sum a log a: q sum r log(qr)
    # better
    H= -np.sum(a*np.log(a)) - l*b*np.log(b)
    B= -np.log(n) - (np.sum(np.log(a)) + l*np.log(b))/n
    return H,B

def fun(x):
    H,B=props(x)
    return [H-h0,B-10]
# bounds q in (0,1), r in (1/7 maybe 1)
for guess in [(0.9999,0.2),(0.999,0.3),(0.99999,0.15),(1-1e-6,0.5),(0.99,0.5)]:
    sol=least_squares(fun,guess,bounds=([0,1/7+1e-12],[1-1e-15,1-1e-12]),xtol=1e-15,ftol=1e-15,gtol=1e-15,max_nfev=10000)
    print(guess, sol.x, fun(sol.x), sol.cost)

"""Construct a probability distribution with forward and backward KL divergences of 10.

For a uniform reference distribution U with n categories, and a model distribution P:

    KL(P || U) = sum_i P_i log(P_i / U_i)
    KL(U || P) = sum_i U_i log(U_i / P_i)

We use a two-level distribution:
  * 7 "high-probability" categories, one with probability q*s and six with
    probability q*(1-s)/6;
  * the remaining n-7 categories all have the same small probability.

The two free parameters q and s are solved numerically so both KL values equal 10.
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import least_squares

N = 150_000
TARGET_KL = 10.0
TOLERANCE = 0.001
NUM_HIGH = 7

# The two constraints can be written as:
#   forward KL = log(N) - H(P) = 10
#   backward KL = -log(N) - E[log(P)] = 10
TARGET_ENTROPY = np.log(N) - TARGET_KL
TARGET_MEAN_LOG = -np.log(N) - TARGET_KL

LOW_COUNT = N - NUM_HIGH


def make_distribution(q: float, s: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Build the distribution from high-group mass q and high-group shape s."""
    high = np.full(NUM_HIGH, q * (1.0 - s) / (NUM_HIGH - 1), dtype=np.float64)
    high[0] = q * s
    low = np.full(LOW_COUNT, (1.0 - q) / LOW_COUNT, dtype=np.float64)
    return np.concatenate((high, low))


def kl_values(q: float, s: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    p = make_distribution(q, s)

    # KL(P || U)
    forward = np.sum(p * np.log(p * N))

    # KL(U || P)
    backward = -np.mean(np.log(N * p))

    return forward, backward


def residuals(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    q, s = x
    forward, backward = kl_values(q, s)
    return np.array([forward - TARGET_KL, backward - TARGET_KL])


# Initial values and feasible bounds.  s > 1/7 makes the high group slightly
# non-uniform, which reduces its entropy to the required value.
x0 = np.array([0.99995, 0.25])
lower = np.array([1e-12, 1.0 / NUM_HIGH + 1e-12])
upper = np.array([1.0 - 1e-12, 1.0 - 1e-12])

solution = least_squares(
    residuals,
    x0,
    bounds=(lower, upper),
    xtol=1e-15,
    ftol=1e-15,
    gtol=1e-15,
    max_nfev=10_000,
)

if not solution.success:
    raise RuntimeError(f"Optimization failed: {solution.message}")

q, s = solution.x
dist = make_distribution(q, s)

forward, backward = kl_values(q, s)
print(f"sum(P)              = {dist.sum():.17g}")
print(f"min(P)              = {dist.min():.17g}")
print(f"KL(P || U)          = {forward:.15f}")
print(f"KL(U || P)          = {backward:.15f}")
print(f"q (high-group mass) = {q:.15f}")
print(f"s (largest shape)   = {s:.15f}")

if dist.min() <= 0.0 or not np.isclose(dist.sum(), 1.0, atol=1e-14):
    raise RuntimeError("Constructed array is not a valid probability distribution")
if abs(forward - TARGET_KL) > TOLERANCE or abs(backward - TARGET_KL) > TOLERANCE:
    raise RuntimeError("KL targets were not met within tolerance")

np.save("/app/dist.npy", dist)
print("Saved /app/dist.npy")
